original_question: Extend the theory of global and local Weyl modules from current and loop algebras to more arbitrary equivariant map Lie algebras. In particular, determine lengths, dimensions, and characters of local Weyl modules in that general setting, and decide whether a suitable form of BGG reciprocity also holds for general EMAs.
target_in_paper: Section 4.3.1(b), “Weyl modules”: the open problem asking to extend to more arbitrary equivariant map Lie algebras the known results on the lengths, dimensions, and characters of local Weyl modules, and to determine whether the BGG reciprocity known for current algebras extends to a more general EMA setting.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper’s Weyl-module open problem in the Lie-EMA setting. In particular, it captures the two exact research directions singled out in the paper: (1) extending known results on local Weyl modules—specifically their lengths, dimensions, and characters—from current/loop-algebra cases to more arbitrary equivariant map Lie algebras, and (2) asking whether a BGG-type reciprocity should also persist in that broader setting.
missing_details: The official target is not a general-EMA problem in the associative/Lie combined sense of Section 4.2; it is specifically the Lie-algebra problem in Section 4.3.1(b).
The ambient object in Section 4.3 is an equivariant map Lie algebra M = M(X, g)^Γ, with g a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero.
The underlying EMA setup from Sections 1 and 4 is X = Spec A affine, A commutative, and Γ finite acting on both X (equivalently A) and g by automorphisms.

In the nearby Weyl-module discussion of Section 3.3, the untwisted reference case assumes g is simple, A is a commutative associative unital algebra, and one fixes a triangular decomposition g = n− ⊕ h ⊕ n+ together with P+ and Q+.

The untwisted global Weyl modules being generalized are W_A(λ), λ in P+, and the untwisted local Weyl modules are W(ψ), where ψ is a finitely supported map X_rat → P+ and λ = sum over x in Supp(ψ) of ψ(x).

The draft says 'extend the theory of global and local Weyl modules,' but the paper is narrower: it notes that definitions already exist in broader settings and asks specifically for extensions of known results on local Weyl-module invariants, plus BGG reciprocity.

If the question is to be fully stand-alone, one should specify that 'length' means module length/composition length (Jordan–Hölder length); the paper’s open-problem bullet does not spell this out, but it is the natural interpretation.

If the question is to be fully stand-alone, one should specify what 'character' means here (most naturally a weight character as a g-module); the survey does not restate this explicitly in the open-problem bullet.

The untwisted local Weyl module W(ψ) is defined nearby by a highest-weight-style generator-and-relations presentation: (n+ ⊗ A)w_ψ = 0, α w_ψ = (sum over x in Supp(ψ) of ψ(x)(α(x))) w_ψ for α in h ⊗ A, and (f_i ⊗ 1)^{λ(h_i)+1} w_ψ = 0 for i in I.

The paper does not restate internally the exact categorical formulation of BGG reciprocity; it only refers to the notion 'described in [10,11]'. So a paper-faithful refinement should ask for an analogue of that current-algebra BGG reciprocity, without inventing a stronger or more specific variant.
refined_question: Let M = M(X, g)^Γ = (g ⊗ A)^Γ be an equivariant map Lie algebra, where X = Spec A is affine, Γ is finite, and the base field is algebraically closed of characteristic 0. In any generality where analogues of the untwisted global Weyl modules W_A(λ) (for λ in P+) and local Weyl modules W(ψ) (for finitely supported ψ : X_rat → P+) are defined, extend to this broader EMA setting the known current/loop-algebra results on the composition lengths, dimensions, and characters of the local Weyl modules, and determine whether an analogue of the current-algebra BGG reciprocity also holds for these equivariant map Lie algebras.
justification: The draft is clearly targeting the open problem in Section 4.3.1(b), not any statement from Section 1: the paper’s wording there is a near-verbatim match for your phrases about local Weyl-module lengths, dimensions, characters, and BGG reciprocity. The nearby context sharpens the scope in two ways. First, Section 4.3 makes clear that the problem is about equivariant map Lie algebras M = M(X, g)^Γ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. Second, Section 3.3 provides the untwisted models W_A(λ) and W(ψ), their parameter sets, and the generator-and-relations description of W(ψ), which show exactly what kind of objects are being generalized. Your draft is slightly broader than the paper because it asks to extend the whole theory of global/local Weyl modules, whereas the survey says definitions already exist in broader settings and isolates the open problem as extending known results on local Weyl-module invariants and BGG reciprocity.
